Chapter 2: How Engrams Form and Shape Behavior.
If you’ve ever wondered why certain emotions, habits, or even aches and pains keep showing up in your life, you’re not alone. Let’s talk about engrams—a fascinating concept that helps explain these stubborn patterns.
An engram is basically a mental recording that happens when you’re in pain, under extreme stress, or even unconscious. But here’s the twist: unlike regular memories, engrams aren’t stored neatly or with any real context. They get tucked away in what’s called the reactive mind—often without you even realizing it.
So, when do these engrams actually form? Picture moments when your logical brain just can’t keep up—maybe during an accident, a heated argument, an illness, or something that really shocks you. At times like these, your mind isn’t analyzing things; instead, your reactive mind just soaks up everything happening around you. Words, sounds, even the tiniest sensations and emotions—they all get recorded, raw and unfiltered.
Here’s a real-world example: imagine a kid who’s feeling sick at school and gets scolded harshly by a teacher. In that stressful, confusing instant, an engram forms. Later in life, facing criticism or feeling unwell—or even just hearing a similar tone of voice—can trigger the same old reaction. Suddenly, the person might feel anxious, defensive, or physically sick, and have no clue why. It’s the engram talking, not the logical mind.
And it’s not just your emotions that get hijacked. Engrams can show up in your body, too. Ever had unexplained headaches, waves of fatigue, or weird aches that seem to come out of nowhere? Sometimes, these are the mind’s way of protecting you from a threat it thinks is real—even when it isn’t.
Now, you might think only dramatic events leave a mark, but that’s not the case. Even small moments—like being teased as a kid, feeling embarrassed in front of friends, or stressing over a looming deadline—can leave behind engrams, especially when you’re feeling vulnerable. Over time, these hidden recordings can quietly steer your reactions, making you avoid certain situations, doubt yourself, or feel stressed for no obvious reason.
Here’s something to really keep in mind: understanding how engrams form gives you a totally new way to look at personal challenges. It means those tough habits or feelings aren’t just about being weak or failing—they often come from old pain stored in the reactive mind. And that’s actually hopeful news. Because when you start addressing these engrams, you open the door to changing patterns that might’ve seemed impossible to budge, leading to better mental and physical health.
